evidence: WHAT THE SOURCE SHOWS (static reading, no run). (1) Scoring policy is the unchanged template: tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gates render/constraints 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; tests/tools/score.py:46-48 computes a weighted sum that is non-decreasing in every dimension, zeroes on a failed gate (line 41-44) and on functional <= 0.05 (line 47, strict '>'). scoring.toml, score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template. Craft (visual 0.2) carries less mass than function. (2) I looked for a dominance inversion, i.e. an app satisfying a strict superset of the public requirements scoring lower, and found none in the text. Every refusal/absence row I read names a same-mechanism success control, so a dead or refuse-everything app cannot collect negative credit: e.g. hro_change_aba 'a desk whose commit never succeeds earns no credit here' (functional/judge.toml:1028), hro_relocation_approval 'a missing or refused operation cannot earn absence credit' (:470), hro_signing_cap 'so a handler that never settles cannot pass' (:596), the 12 hro_change_prepare_*/commit_* rows 'after a successful Finance prepare/commit control' (:1181-1280), hro_anon_read_* 'A missing populated authenticated control proves nothing' (:704), hro_live_stale_mark control state plus the non-invalidating direction (:1334), hro_pol_live_keeps_entries 'If no update arrives within15 seconds there is nothing to observe: give0' (polish/judge.toml:23). Polish rows that lean on functional behaviour do not reward the weaker app more: hro_pol_change_recovery lets a non-enforcing app reach the same credit by another genuine refusal, never more (polish/judge.toml:50). Both gates ask only for sign-in and one requisition plus one PENDING offer read back in a fresh context (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-26), which the brief requires of every conforming app, so I found no gate that a stronger app fails by design. Three conditional passes exist (hro_draft_eligibility :650 'If the optional history is omitted ... this condition is satisfied', P5a 'no such claims satisfies', hro_change_intent_key commit-carries-none leg); the first is weight 0.01 of 64.404 (0.016% of functional) and none lets a strictly worse app pass a strictly better one. (3) Weight arrangement inside functional (computed from judge.toml, 152 criteria, total weight 64.40418425): underlying offer desk 20.004 (31.1%), coordinated-change engine 28.9 (44.9%), change-desk working behaviour hro_desk_/hro_live_/hro_whatif/hro_entries 13.5 (21.0%), hro_keep_* 2.0 (3.1%). The seven rows that own the brief's headline integrity promises (hro_change_stale_leaf, _aba, _retry_concurrent, _overlap, _retry_later, _retry_restart, _intent_key) total 10.5 = 16.3% of functional = 9.8% of reward. See counterexample field for the ordering this produces between two non-dominated apps; it is a judgement about which app is 'worse', overlaps check 44, and is not a demonstrated dominance inversion, so I do not call it a Fail. WHAT IS MISSING. raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent. The golden has NOT been scripted through every Functional criterion'. Its 10 artifacts hash-match and their matching_source_files match the frozen solution bytes, but they are scripted golden observations only; none is a mutated-weak-app or configured-judge run. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-ordering runtime record before local clearance, and the internal workbook annotation on this row is 'we need to monitor this one'. No such record exists for this input hash, so monotonicity of the measured reward is unmeasured. One ordering risk can only be settled by a run: the functional judge must work 152 criteria in one batched 9000 s session (about 59 s per criterion) and polish has 900 s for five multi-context scenarios, and all three scored prompts map an exhausted budget to binary0 / Likert1 ('NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation', functional/prompt.md:15, polish/prompt.md:18, visual/prompt.md:16). A complete app gives the judge more to exercise than an app whose change desk is absent, so rows unreached for the better app score 0 while the weaker app loses nothing extra; and tests/test.sh:224-226 leaves reward 0 if the scored suite itself exits non-zero. I did not determine how harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 reports a per-judge timeout and I have no timing measurement, so I state this as an unmeasured risk, not an observed inversion. Timeouts are unchanged from the template and I recommend no change without a measurement.
counterexample: Not a dominance counterexample; an unmeasured ordering concern derived from the weights only. App W: complete polished change desk (pre-save figures, live marks, what-if, unsent entries, focus, recovery) whose commit never refuses a stale or ABA preview, is not safe under concurrent or overlapping commits and re-settles on retry. If judged as written it loses the seven integrity rows (10.5/64.404): functional 0.837, polish up to 1.0 because hro_pol_change_recovery allows another genuine refusal and hro_pol_uncertain_commit says 'exact duplicate-settlement counts belong to Functional' -> reward 0.702 + 0.2*visual. App S: financially correct offer desk and coordinated-change engine (all 28.9 engine rows and all base rows) with a plain form and no live update, what-if, unsent-entry persistence or focus handling: loses desk rows 13.5/64.404 -> functional 0.790; polish keeps only hro_pol_change_recovery and hro_pol_uncertain_commit (5/12) -> reward 0.558 + 0.2*visual. At equal visual, W outscores S by about 0.145 although W can pay people twice and commit out-of-date previews, the first things the brief asks to prevent (instruction.md:3). Both apps miss public requirements, so which is 'worse' is a judgement; these figures are arithmetic on the shipped weights, not judge output.
suggested_fix: Produce the hash-bound reward-ordering record the review policy requires: run the full configured verifier on the golden and on at least two mutated apps of clearly ordered quality (for example golden; golden with freshness/idempotency enforcement removed; golden with the live desk behaviours removed; a requisition/offer-only app) and confirm the rewards order as intended and that the judge reaches every protocol within the existing budgets. If the owner agrees that W-over-S is the wrong order, rebalance task-specific per-criterion weights so the integrity rows outweigh the desk-behaviour rows (coordinate with row 44); do not touch scoring.toml, score.py, test.sh or timeouts.
